title: A nonlinear geometric-mean map exactly contracts prime-family eta
question: After ruling out a fixed Markov channel, can a positive nonlinear arithmetic operation realize the derived horizontal contraction?

verdict.conclusion: The normalized geometric interpolation G_c(q) proportional to q^c p_0^(1-c) is a positive nonlinear map on prime-power laws. Its fixed points are p_0 conditioned on support; since the actual zero mixture has full support, its only possible fixed point is p_0. Thus G_c(P_xi)=P_xi would prove RH; no arithmetic theorem establishes that fixed-point relation.

map.parameterMap: a=2+2eta -> a_c=2+c(a-2), equivalently eta -> c eta
map.fixedPointProof: G_c(q)=q iff q is p_0 conditioned on its support S; full support S gives q=p_0
map.klDerivative: d/dt D(G_t(q)||p_0)=t Var_(G_t(q))(log(q/p_0))>=0; moving from t=1 down to c<1 strictly lowers KL unless q/p_0 is constant on q's support, i.e. q is p_0 conditioned on its support; in particular it is strict for full-support q != p_0

actualXiGate.whyNotDerived: Every zero-feature p_eta is strictly positive on every prime power, so their positive mixture P_xi has full support. The completed explicit formula is linear and signed; no same-xi prime-side identity proves invariance of this aggregate under G_c.

scope: This constructs a nonlinear positive map on probability ledgers; it is not a Markov kernel on prime indices, not a holomorphic deformation of xi, and not evidence that the actual zero ledger is invariant.
status: The contraction is realized exactly on the prime feature family. The fixed-point link to the actual xi zero mixture remains RH-equivalent and unproved.
